title: Operadic correspondences and their left Kan extensions
statement:
Use the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], the inert maps and operadic axioms of [lem-coef-inert-operad-color-reconstruction], cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and coherent diagrams and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Relative limit cones and joins have the meaning of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Here a generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad means an inner fibration satisfying the inert-lift, Segal fiber-product, and incidence-diagram axioms of [lem-coef-inert-operad-color-reconstruction], with arbitrary zero fiber; a Kan zero fiber is required only where explicitly stated below. Let $S$ be a small quasicategory. An $S$-family of generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads is a categorical fibration $\pi:\mathcal M\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\times S$ satisfying the following conditions. Here categorical fibration means an inner fibration which lifts equivalences with prescribed source. For each $s\in S$, its fiber $\mathcal M_s\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad; every inert base arrow has a cocartesian lift for the projection $\mathcal M_s\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ within this fiber. These lifts give relative $\pi$-limit Segal cones: for $x$ over $([r],s)$, take the inert restrictions to its $r$ consecutive edges $[1]$ and its $r+1$ vertices $[0]$, together with the endpoint arrows from each edge to its two vertices; the cone from $x$ to this incidence diagram is a $\pi$-limit. For $r=0$ this diagram consists of the single vertex $[0]$. A map from such a family to a monoidal infinity category $\mathcal V^\otimes$ of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] is a functor over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ preserving these fiberwise inert edges. Let $\mathcal E_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}_{/\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mathcal M,\mathcal V^\otimes)$ on those functors, with coherent transformations over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$.

A correspondence is an $S$-family for $S=\Delta^1$; put $\mathcal A=\mathcal M_0$ and $\mathcal B=\mathcal M_1$. It is constant over $[0]$ if $\mathcal M_{[0]}\to\Delta^1$ is a cocartesian fibration classified by an equivalence $\mathcal A_{[0]}\simeq\mathcal B_{[0]}$. For the active-slice and Kan-extension definitions below, assume that the correspondence is constant over $[0]$ and that both these fibers are spaces. An edge is active if its image in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is opposite to a map preserving endpoints. Write $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{act}}$ for the wide subcategory with exactly the active edges. For $b\in\mathcal B_{[1]}$ set $J_b=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{act}})_{/b}$, where the slice consists of active arrows with target $b$ and their coherent commuting triangles, and its map to $\mathcal M$ evaluates the source.

For an active diagram $T:K\to\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ and an active cocone $T\to v$ with $v\in\mathcal V$, call the cocone weakly operadically colimiting if restriction gives an equivalence from the space of active arrows $v\to w$ to the space of coherent active cocones $T\to w$ for every $w\in\mathcal V$. It is operadically colimiting if both $L\oplus T\to L\oplus v$ and $T\oplus R\to v\oplus R$ are weakly operadically colimiting for every finite tuple $L$ or $R$, including the empty tuple. Here weakly operadically colimiting for a tuple apex uses active arrows from that tuple to $w$; $\oplus$ is concatenation under the monoidal Segal identifications, including the empty tuple. An inert-preserving functor $H:\mathcal M\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an operadic left Kan extension of $H|_{\mathcal A}$ if, for every color $b$ of $\mathcal B$, its induced cocone $J_b\to H(b)$ is operadically colimiting. These are the mapping-space forms of the operadic cocone definitions; no existence of colimits or extensions is included in this definition.

The statement already expands the family, correspondence, active slice, weak and operadic colimit, and operadic left Kan extension data; each prerequisite notion is supplied by an existing DAG node. Second reading corrects two source mismatches: families allow an arbitrary zero fiber, and the Kan-extension predicate requires a correspondence constant over [0]. It also specifies active slices and mapping-space language; no proof steps or new nodes are introduced.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q04-ea50af79f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its 6 statement dependencies, its 5 citers and the unit in full, and compared the item against the Gepner-Haugseng paper, arXiv:1312.3178v4. The PDF was fetched online and its text extracted in /tmp; I read Def. 3.1.13 on p.21 and Defs. A.2.1-A.3.3 with Rem. A.2.2 on pp.87-90. Generalized operad: GH 3.1.13 has three axioms and no Kan condition on the zero fiber. The item correctly takes only axioms (i)-(iii) from lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability and leaves out that node's Kan clause; the N([1]) x Delta^op counterexample checks out. S-family (A.3.1): categorical fibration (defined inline as inner fibration plus isofibration), inert cocartesian lifts in each fiber, Segal cones over the incidence diagram that are pi-limits for the full projection, and each fiber an operad. The incidence diagram is right, including the single vertex at r=0. Constant over [0] (A.3.2) matches. Kan extension (A.3.3): the item now requires both constancy and Kan zero fibers, as GH does; the empty-source example shows constancy is a genuine extra hypothesis. J_b = A x_M (M_act)_/b with the source leg, tested at every b in B_[1], matches GH. Weak operadic colimit: GH asks for a categorical equivalence of left fibrations over O_[1] (Rem. A.2.2). Fiber by fiber this is the item's condition that active arrows v->w match active cocones T->w; I checked the fiber identification. Operadic colimit: one-sided L+T and T+R for every tuple, including the empty one, as in GH; no existence claim. Only harmless narrowings: S is small and the target is a monoidal V^otimes rather than a general operad; every user uses Delta^1 and a monoidal target. All 6 dependencies are used for what they say. No duplicate definition node exists in the DAG and there are no new nodes. All 5 citers stay valid after the correction. All three kinds of Mathlib search were run with a no-match verdict; no SGA is cited. This is a definition, not a target, so there is no base-change morphism to compare. No fixes, no dropped nodes, no tool_uses.
